title: Build together: website inquiries and the website tab
goal: Take the fifth piece through the six steps, and slow down on the test. You leave with website inquiries in your pipeline, each with its source, and a build you tested with three checks you read first.
you_need: The class starter for week 5, unzipped
The Claude app or Claude Code
Optional: a form export from your own website, saved as CSV

steps.do: Design: Double-click Launch, press Start the six steps, and read the design note for website inquiries.
steps.see: The question it answers: what came in through the website, and is the website doing its job?
steps.tip: The form is the front door. Know where each lead came from.

steps.do: Design: Before you build, read the three checks in step 4. Say out loud the numbers each one expects.
steps.see: 8 rows in the file: 5 to add, 2 duplicates, 1 held back.
steps.tip: A check written before the build is a test. A check written after is a description.

steps.do: Prompt: Press Copy the build prompt, paste it into the Claude app or Claude Code, and send. Save the file as week-5-website.js in the pieces folder, and say yes to replace.
steps.see: Your computer asks whether to replace week-5-website.js.
steps.tip: Nothing is connected to your website. The export comes in by hand, and that is the point.

steps.do: Review: Press I saved the file. Look again. Read the page against the design note and find the one thing it got wrong.
steps.see: Two tabs: Inquiries, with a box for the form export, and Website, with the three-second test and the search numbers.
steps.tip: Look for a number that could not have come from the file. There must not be one.

steps.do: Test: Press Load the sample file, then Check this file. Read the sum, then press Add 5 to the pipeline. Then load and check the same file again.
steps.see: 5 plus 2 plus 1 is 8. The pipeline goes from 8 deals to 13. The second time, 0 to add.
steps.tip: Count before and after, and explain any gap. If you cannot explain it, stop.

steps.do: Ship: Press How it was built, and in step 5 type your runbook line: the step, the sign it worked, how to undo it.
steps.see: Three short answers, saved as you type.
steps.tip: For example: each Monday I export the form and check it here. The sum matches the file. Start over puts the sample back.

steps.do: Log: In step 6, type what changed and why, then press Add to my change log.
steps.see: Your change log has one more line.
steps.tip: Next Wednesday: the content calendar, and a post graphic from your own Canva template.

real_life: This week: export the form submissions from your own website as a CSV file. Press My business, open Website, and drop the file in.
Read the sum before you press Add. Rows in the file equals added plus duplicates plus held back.
Open the Website tab and run the three-second test on your own home page. Ask someone who has never seen it.
if_it_breaks: The AI is slow, or the page does not show after you saved the file: take the finished week-5-website.js from the pieces folder of the complete project, save it in your pieces folder, and keep going.
No rows were found in your export: the first row needs headings such as Name, Email, Phone and Message. Open sample-form-export.csv in the class folder to see the shape.
The counts look wrong: press Start over with the sample data here and in the pipeline, then run the checks again.
